# Source: teambuilding notes (foundational)

**Do not edit this file.** It is a near-verbatim record of notes the user took
from masterclass videos by a Pokémon world champion, provided 2026-09-08. It
exists so that any later rewrite of the working reference files can be diffed
against what the source actually said.

Everything below this header is the source as written, including its own
spelling and shorthand. It is **generic VGC**, not Champions-specific: some
examples name Pokémon that are not in the Champions roster. Those are
corrected in the working files, never here.

**Working files built on this:** `reference/archetypes.md`,
`reference/speed-control.md`, `reference/roles.md`,
`reference/team-evaluation.md`.

---

Team starting points
- specific strategy: e.g. Trick room, weather, ect
- Around specific pokemon:  e.g. a specific mega, or specific core of multiple
- Using/refining an already exiting team  (self built or lifted from somewhere else)

Speed control is important, often the most important!
-common strategy starting point
--KOing an opponent before they can move is pretty good
--so is moving first to reduce bad luck chances (flinch/status effect)
--(not always need to be centerpoint though)
-forms of control
--priority moves
--items (choice scarf)
--paralysis
--certain abilities (e.g. clorophyll, swift swim)
--moves that reduce speed (e.g. ice wind, cotton spore)
--moves that change speed order (e.g trick room, tailwind)
--really fast pokemon (e.g. areodactyl, dragapult)

Strategies

-Tailwind
--saving tailwind for later turns can be crucial
--usually only need one tailwind user
--helps to have strong attackers with spread moves (e.g. garchaop earthquake)
--tailwind setter need to be able to contribute more than just tailwind
--fakeout can be helpful to set up tailwind, but fake out user needs to be able to do more as well.

-Trick Room
--these tips are specific for HARD trick room, not just carrying trick  room on a pokemon
--trick room has extremely low priority, need to have plan for setup (fake out, follow me, ect)
--usually run two TR setter, but can run 1 depending on meta
--slow strong attackers with spread moves (e.g torkal eruption)
--need plan for getting sweeper in after TR is set up.

-Good Stuff (Balance)
--Just bring good pokemon
--Very Flexible team
--Need Good Defensive/Offensive Synergy, can easily switch around
--often run 1-2 pokemon for specific common matchups

-Weather
--can set via ability (most common) or move, usually only one setter
--Have plans for other weather conditions (can overwrite)
--Bulky mons can help to swap in/out for resetting
--Rain tends to be more bulky
--On Sun team usually 1 clorophyll pokemon
--Sand has the weakest benefits,, but stringes setter (Tyranitar)
--Tyranitar need support (slow and lots of weaknesses)
--Snow most benefits from auroura veilf or blizzard usage
--snow is good counter weather (setters are mostly good standalone), dont overindex on it
--Team should NOT just be 6 pokemon that benefit from thew weather, otherwise you will have trouble playing outside of it



Building Around Specific Pokémon

--Know what the pokemon does well, vs where it struggles
---if it needs speed control
---type weaknesses/strengths
---attacking stat (atk vs spa), or support plan
--Build one pokemon at a time, each choice affects the next, be very intentional
--know WHY you are adding a pokemon and how it helps the core pokemon, dont just add good ones
--look for partners that tick multiple boxes

Using an Existing Team
--Feel free to use teams made by others
--dont hesitate to change the team (moves, stats, even swap a pokemon out) based on your playstyle/preferences



Other Rules

--Use "Good" Pokémon
---How well does it do against common pokemon
---what are its stats/moves/ability
---what role is it filling?
---is there another pokemon legal that fills that role better? (e.g. Urshifu is mostly just a better Palafin)
---Does NOT mean "bad" pokemon cant be used, but it is harder and required more work
---usage and win rates are a great easy way to get an idea of how "good" a pokemon is, but not authoritative, sometimes a low usage pokemon is an undiscovered gem
---whether a pokmeon is "good" or "bad" can change on the meta (e.g. if there lots of counter to it currently)

--Mega Pokémon Tips
---Megas are strong!
---Can be a great centerpiece for a team, make sure youre getting the most out of it and have its weaknesses (type and playstyle) covered
---Dont feel forced to center gameplan around mega every game, sometimes you can leave it behind
---Its okay to run 2 megas on one team! but probably not more, and at least 1 in mega-allowed metas

Choosing the right moveset / Roles
--Makes sense to pick the ROLE first, then the moveset/SP spread depending on that
---some pokemon are more flexible than others, some are stuck in certain roles
--What role does your pokemon fill? Usually defines the set (but CAN change)
---Offensive - STAB 1, STAB2, Coverage/Setup/Support, Protect
---Defensive - Support 1, Support 2, STAB, Support3/Protect

Improving a team
--Teambuilding is HARD, dont expect easy results!
--Analyze why you lost
---Bad luck
---played badly
---missing tools/moves
--Iterative cycle, battle->adjust->battle->adjust until youre happy
